extra.message: SQL injection in overdueDigestForTimezone(): the client-controlled 'timezone' cookie (read in ReportsController.dueTodayByTimezone, reachable by ANY authenticated user) is concatenated directly into a raw SQL string passed to prisma.$queryRawUnsafe at line 339. An attacker can set dashboard_timezone to a crafted value and read arbitrary tables/columns (password hashes, internal notes, PII) or tamper data. A parameterized query or an allow-list of timezones is required.

cwe: CWE-89: SQL Injection

extra.message: OS command injection in normalizeIntakeForm(): presentationFormat is taken from the unvalidated request body (AttachmentsController.normalizeIntakeForm, reachable by any authenticated user who can access an attachment, including customers for their own tickets) and interpolated into a shell command string executed with execSync: `pandoc ${srcPath} -o ${outPath} -t ${presentationFormat}`. A value such as 'pdf; cat /etc/passwd > /tmp/x;' executes arbitrary commands with the server's privileges. Use execFileSync with an argument array and a whitelist (as renderCaseFileBundle does).

extra.message: Mass-assignment / privilege escalation in restoreWorkspaceLayout() (route POST /auth/workspace-layout/restore/:exportCode, guarded only by JwtAuthGuard, so reachable by any authenticated user including customer_user). The user-supplied exportCode is base64-decoded, JSON-parsed, and the resulting object is spread into the Prisma UserUpdateInput (lines 199-200) without an allow-list. A customer can supply {"role":"support_admin"} (or set organizationId/teamId/isActive/passwordHash) and escalate their own account to admin or take over other accounts. extra.message: Unauthenticated disclosure of internal notes in previewPartnerHandoff() (public route POST /tickets/partner-handoff/preview). The caller simply claims membershipStatus='enterprise' and full internal notes for the referenced ticket are returned. Ticket references are sequential (TCK-10001...) so an anonymous attacker can enumerate references and read staff-only internal notes across all organizations. The verified variant (previewPartnerHandoffVerified) correctly checks the organization's plan on file.

extra.message: Missing authorization on GET /kb/manage/editorial-archive. Unlike every other KB management route, this handler has no @Roles(...) restriction (and the controller declares none at class level), so any authenticated user - including customer_user - can list internal-visibility and draft/in_review/archived knowledge base articles together with the author's email. Draft and internal KB articles are explicitly meant to be staff-only.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: Unrestricted file upload / path traversal in uploadBrandingLogo() (route POST /organizations/:id/branding-logo, customer_user role). The uploaded file is written to the web-accessible public/branding directory using the client-supplied file.originalname with no MIME/extension/size validation and no path containment, so a customer can write arbitrary content (e.g. an HTML file) under an arbitrary name, including '..' segments that escape the branding directory (CWE-22 + CWE-434). uploadBrandingLogoSafe() is the hardened variant (random stored name, size + MIME allow-list, private directory).

extra.message: Mass assignment in updatePortalProfile() (route POST /organizations/:id/portal-profile). The entire request body is spread into the Prisma organization.update data with no allow-list, so a customer editing their portal profile can set any Organization column including plan (self-upgrade to 'enterprise'), domain, and notes (overwriting compliance/billing records stored there). updatePortalProfileSafe() only writes name/domain.

extra.message: Weak one-time access codes enable account takeover. requestPortalAccess() generates a 6-digit numeric code with Math.random() and stores it for 10 minutes in an in-memory map; verifyPortalAccess() (public route POST /auth/portal-access/verify) applies no rate limiting or attempt cap, so an attacker who knows a target email (seeded/README accounts are public) can brute-force the 10^6 code space within the validity window and mint a session for that customer account. The same Math.random() 6-digit pattern is used for backup-channel codes (line 234).

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: Unauthenticated escalation ownership takeover in acceptPartnerOwnershipHandoff() (public route POST /escalations/:id/partner-handoff/accept). Authorization relies solely on the caller-supplied x-partner-clearance header checked with loose equality (clearanceLevel == 5) against the stub PartnerEntitlementClient which always returns access:true, so any anonymous caller can send x-partner-clearance: 5 and reassign an escalation to an arbitrary ownerId.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Customer-continuity codes are generated with Math.random() (5 base-36 chars) rather than a CSPRNG. verifyCustomerContinuity() is public and returns the full ticket with all replies after only this code; with sequential, guessable ticket references (TCK-10001...) and a 30-minute validity window the code space is weak. randomBytes() is already used elsewhere in the same service and should be used here.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
